description: Editorial coverage notes, not completed experiments. Related records retain their own bounds and outcomes. Proposed extensions have not been run.

records.title: Choosing a sentence and deriving its key
records.coverage: An unrestricted additive key can be calculated from any equal-length ciphertext and proposed plaintext. A readable output alone cannot choose between those keys. Related seed controls test a narrower, predefined key generator.
records.needed: Specify a key-generation rule independently of the desired sentence, freeze its parameters, and predict text not used to choose them.
records.next_test: Demonstrate several incompatible plaintexts for one synthetic ciphertext, then compare their predictive power under a fixed key rule.

records.title: Changing decoding rules to keep producing words
records.coverage: Existing tests cover selected alignment and F-rune reset rules. They do not cover arbitrary skips, resets or switching operations whenever a word stops looking plausible.
records.needed: Define the permitted choices, their maximum number and the rule that selects them. Apply the same selection procedure to controls.
records.next_test: Compare fixed decoding with bounded adaptive decoding on original and shuffled inputs, recording every intervention.

records.title: Finding short words among many candidates
records.coverage: Search-maximum and scorer controls address selection effects. Several cipher sweeps only compare nine specific known openings; their failures do not exclude other plaintexts.
records.needed: Fix the dictionary or language score, minimum length, offsets and number of candidates before inspecting outputs. Compare the best result with equally large control searches.
records.next_test: Measure how often short dictionary words occur as candidate counts and searched offsets increase.

records.title: Anagrams and freely rearranged words
records.coverage: Anagram repetition and fixed reversals have records. Those do not test independently choosing an arrangement for every word to form a sentence.
records.needed: Declare token boundaries, allowed permutations, dictionary and handling of unused letters. Distinguish one shared transposition rule from separate word-by-word choices.
records.next_test: Enumerate dictionary alternatives for each token and compare sentence-selection freedom with matched controls.

records.title: Words or sentences chosen to match prime sums
records.coverage: Selected word-sum audits check specific supplied matches and rune segmentations. They do not establish how many alternative words or sentences fit the same totals.
records.needed: Fix the vocabulary, spelling normalization, rune segmentation rules and target selection. Count competing matches rather than reporting only the preferred wording.
records.next_test: Build a bounded dictionary collision census with all alternatives retained for each target total.

records.title: Searching arithmetic until a familiar number appears
records.coverage: Bounded number and prime-sum tests exist. A search allowing unrestricted expressions, bases, reversals and constants has no specified completion condition.
records.needed: List inputs, operations, constants, bases and maximum expression depth. Define equivalent expressions and the target list before searching.
records.next_test: Enumerate one fixed expression grammar and compare target hits with equally sized control target sets.

records.title: Choosing grids, spirals and reading paths
records.coverage: Simple row/column routes and a selected totient-map route are documented. The LP2-49–51 directional prime-path count now has two conditional shuffle controls; arbitrary grid sizes, padding, origins and path choices remain outside those tests.
records.needed: Fix dimensions, padding, starting cells, allowed paths and tie-breaking. Count the whole family searched, including variants that looked unpromising.
records.next_test: Enumerate a finite route family with identical selection and scoring on original and control inputs.

records.title: Trying books or philosophical texts as keys
records.coverage: The Emerson record reproduces a historical book cipher. It does not test arbitrary referenced books as keys to unsolved pages.
records.needed: Name exact editions and file hashes, encoding rules, offsets and key operation. Specify how books were selected before reading candidate plaintext.
records.next_test: Compare a fixed set of candidate books with unrelated control books under the same bounded offset search.

records.title: Selecting interrupters or reset positions
records.coverage: Two LP2-54–55 records test particular F-rune feedback rules. Neither establishes coverage of all interrupters, pages or key-reset systems.
records.needed: Specify which symbols trigger which state changes, whether the trigger consumes a key position, and whether the same rule applies throughout.
records.next_test: Compare a predeclared small reset-rule family with controls and an untouched continuation.

records.title: Changing separators, headings or page joins
records.coverage: Image-row coverage and word-based tests exist, but an exhaustive experiment across all disputed separators and page joins has not been published.
records.needed: Identify image-supported alternatives, preserve original text, and declare how each version changes tokens or key resets. Do not repair text solely to improve a candidate.
records.next_test: Compare the same decoding and statistics across a fixed list of documented transcription variants.

records.title: AI-generated translations and interpretations
records.coverage: No published record here tests whether an AI distinguishes genuine decipherment from plausible interpretation. Language statistics and scorer controls are related background, not that experiment.
records.needed: Freeze model version, prompt, sampling settings, attempts and an objective scoring rule. Include blinded shuffled inputs and known-answer controls; retain every output.
records.next_test: Run a small blinded comparison measuring verifiable recovery and false claims, rather than fluency or thematic plausibility.

records.title: Searching for images through processing and overlays
records.coverage: OutGuess and image-row detection tests cover specific procedures. They do not exclude hidden content under other processing, or establish that an interpreted shape is intentional.
records.needed: Bound transforms, thresholds, rotations, alignment and candidate selection. Apply the same search to controls and distinguish measured features from perceived subjects.
records.next_test: Test one finite processing family using blinded image controls and a declared feature-detection criterion.
